policy_title: Protect State Pension Triple Lock and Review Workplace Pensions
stated: Labour will retain the triple lock for the state pension, ensuring security in retirement. They will also adopt reforms to workplace pensions to deliver better outcomes for UK savers and pensioners, and a pensions review will consider further steps to improve retirement security and increase productive investment in the UK economy.

source.quote: Our system of state, private, and workplace pensions provide the basis for security in retirement. Labour will retain the triple lock for the state pension. We will also adopt reforms to workplace pensions to deliver better outcomes for UK savers and pensioners. Our pensions review will consider what further steps are needed to improve security in retirement, as well as to increase productive investment in the UK economy.

bearing_set.reason: Retaining the triple lock directly affects state pension adequacy and pensioner poverty; the pensions review explicitly targets retirement security for savers and pensioners.

The triple lock is one of the largest single welfare spending commitments; retaining it carries a substantial, OBR-modelled ongoing fiscal cost that materially affects the funded/borrowed balance and the debt path.

The pensions review explicitly names increasing productive investment in the UK economy as a goal; redirecting pension assets toward domestic productive investment (akin to Mansion House-style reforms) has a plausible, concrete mechanism for raising business investment and productivity — a core O13 indicator.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: O8 is the primary designed-for outcome; O12 captures the non-negligible fiscal cost of retaining the triple lock; O13 reflects the explicitly stated productive-investment objective of the pensions review. No material bearing on O14 (the distributional effect within pensioners and across generations is real but secondary and does not clearly move the Gini or the top-to-bottom gap in a directionally clean way).
